channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: After a decade of community pressure, LA bans oil drilling for good
item.description: Los Angeles has banned oil drilling after a decade of pressure from residents living beside the wells. Evidence: Now policy. How you can help: Turn up at a council meeting on a health issue in your neighbourhood; steady attendance counts. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Infant Goes from 110 Seizures a Day to Seizure-Free with Experimental Treatment
item.description: A baby in Dubai who had about 110 seizures a day is seizure-free after an experimental drug. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: After the 2023 fires, Maui is testing tourism that has visitors help restore land and culture. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: On your next trip, give a day to a local restoration project. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: National Trust takes back land for nature restoration
item.description: The National Trust is taking back a site to restore it, create wildlife habitat and open green space. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: How two Princeton graduates built the world’s first microplastics removal system
item.description: Two graduates built a system that removes microplastics at wastewater plants before water is released. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Wash synthetic clothes less often, on cooler and shorter cycles, to shed fewer fibres. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: China Switches on World’s Biggest Example of New, Cheap Green Energy Storage
item.description: The largest liquid-air energy storage plant yet built is running in western China, banking renewable power. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 100-Year-Old ‘Store Mom’ Surprised With Her First Birthday Party
item.description: Staff at the store where a 100-year-old walks each day threw her the first surprise party of her life. How you can help: Learn the name of someone you see every day and ask how they are. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘There’s a Georgia O’Keeffe in the Closet’ – Words that Led to Painting’s Joyous Rediscovery
item.description: A lost Georgia O'Keeffe painting turned up in a family closet during a clear-out. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Brave Teens Execute Paddleboard Rescue of Flooded Neighbors – ‘Faith in Humanity Restored’
item.description: Teenagers paddled through Florida floodwater to bring a neighbour and her son to safety. How you can help: Swap phone numbers with neighbours before storm season and check on them when water rises. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
item.description: Crows make visual decisions in about 235 milliseconds, twice as fast as humans and monkeys. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
item.description: An AI model predicts what a blind man sees through his brain implant, making bionic vision more precise. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
item.description: A familiar tropical butterfly is three species, one new to science, told apart by ultraviolet wing patterns. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: Moss panels are being tried on city walls to cool streets and clean air, an idea that began in Aachen. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Historic US ocean liner sinks near Florida to become world’s largest artificial reef
item.description: The liner SS United States was sunk off Destin to become the largest artificial reef in the world. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: For Centuries, Visitors Walked Right by 280 Unseen Ice Age Cave Paintings
item.description: About 280 Ice Age engravings were found in a Spanish cave that visitors had walked past for centuries. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Brown Bear Population in Spain Doubles With Incredible Increase of its Breeding Range
item.description: Cantabrian brown bears have doubled to about 370 in twenty years and now roam 6,500 square miles. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘I pulled him out, I heard more screaming’ – How a Cadet Saved a Father and Son from Drowning
item.description: A merchant marine cadet pulled a father and his son from a pool and both survived. How you can help: Take a CPR class; many community pools and first aid groups run short courses. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Paralysis Could Not Stop Her: How This 84-year-old Made Good on Her Musical Promise
item.description: An 84-year-old who arrived at a nursing home paralysed now plays piano for its residents. How you can help: Offer to play music or read aloud at a care home near you; many welcome volunteers. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Prince Bashangezi turned personal loss into peer tutoring for refugee students
item.description: A young man who lost schooling in lockdown set up peer tutoring for refugee students. How you can help: Offer an hour a week to tutor at a local school or refugee support group. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Brazil releases the world’s first fossil fuel phaseout roadmap
item.description: Brazil published the first national roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
item.description: A digital twin of the Webb telescope cleared away glare and revealed a planet hidden in its images. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: ‘Nothing short of a miracle’ – Rescuers Find Boy with Autism Missing for 3 Days
item.description: A six-year-old autistic boy missing for three days in Kentucky was found safe by volunteer searchers. How you can help: Join a local volunteer search and rescue team; most train new members. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Jimmy Carter’s Georgia farm acquired by conservation group planning to open it to public
item.description: A conservation group bought Jimmy Carter's family farm to protect the land and open it to the public. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: A Viral Video Led Strangers to Raise $76,000 for a Full-Time Caregiver
item.description: Strangers who saw a doorbell video raised over $76,000 for a full-time caregiver. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: World’s Driest Desert Erupts into Record-Breaking Bloom Boom (LOOK)
item.description: Rain has brought some 200 species into flower across Chile's Atacama, the largest bloom recorded there. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Paleontologists discover “one-in-a-million” fossil with 450-million-year-old soft tissue
item.description: A 450-million-year-old fossil of a starfish relative has kept its soft tissue. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
item.description: Four NASA volunteers walked out after more than a year in a simulated Mars habitat, mission complete. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: After 40 years, CERN finds evidence of a one-in-10-billion particle decay
item.description: After a 40-year search, CERN has evidence of a particle decay that happens once in 10 billion. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Electric ferries that fly above water are arriving in the US
item.description: Electric ferries that rise on hydrofoils, using far less energy, are starting service in US cities. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Man’s Halloween Skeletons Prove Perfect Treat to Woman Battling Breast Cancer
item.description: A man's yard of Halloween skeletons became the bright spot on a woman's weekly drive to cancer treatment. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: Colleges are adding play corners, childcare help and flexible advising so student parents can finish degrees. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Interpreting Autistic Cues Is Difficult, a Teen Built an App That’s Helping Hundreds of Families
item.description: A teenager built an app to read his autistic cousin's cues; over 700 families in 12 countries now use it. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer
item.description: A UCLA study found a natural molecule may ease brain fog and fatigue after breast cancer treatment. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
item.description: NASA set out a plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with an orbital test in 2027. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: An ancient ocean full of giant predators reveals a surprising twist in evolution
item.description: Fossils in Colombia show an ancient sea crowded with giant reptiles and sharks living side by side. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
item.description: Ancient Europe was open woodland and flowering meadow grazed by large animals, not unbroken forest. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
item.description: With 7% of the sky surveyed, the Rubin Observatory has already found two unknown companions of the Milky Way. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing
item.description: In Juneau, where little food can be grown, neighbours keep each other fed by sharing what they catch and gather. How you can help: Share surplus garden produce or a catch with the people next door. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years
item.description: Chemical traces of blood were confirmed inside dinosaur bones 115 million years old. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Don't miss: Meteor showers, fireballs, and a supermoon light up November's night sky
item.description: November skies offer meteor fireballs, Mars beside Jupiter and a supermoon. How you can help: Step outside on a clear night this month, away from street lights, and look up for ten minutes. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: At a Montana guest ranch, autistic adults work as wranglers, guides, cooks and concierges. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: ‘It’s all God’s creation’: farmers continue a ‘Jewishly inspired’ agrarian tradition
item.description: A growing number of Jewish Americans are finding purpose and community through small-scale farming. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew is moving 1,300 plants to safety so its Victorian Palm House can be restored. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: First dinosaur bone from Antarctica found in a drawer
item.description: A fossil collected in 1985 and left in a drawer turns out to be the first dinosaur bone found in Antarctica. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
